reason: Curative/therapeutic claim wording maps to a drug intent under Drugs & Cosmetics Act 1940 (ASU rules).
Solvent/hydroalcoholic extraction combined with therapeutic purpose suggests a concentrated medicinal product rather than food.
Daily-dietary purpose + structure-function claims + classical aqueous preparation aligns with the Ayurveda Aahara food frame.
source: FSSAI Food Safety and Standards (Ayurveda Aahara) Regulations, 2022

reason: Wellness-only claims in food-type dosage forms fit the Aahara category.

Classical dosage forms (Vati, Kwatha, Churna, Taila, Asava-Arishtha) with medicinal intent default to the ASU drug frame; the same form carrying only wellness claims moves to the Aahara/nutraceutical pathway.
Capsule/tablet form carrying a health claim points to a proprietary Ayurvedic medicine product licence path.
source: Drugs and Cosmetics Act (Schedule Z proprietary Ayurveda medicines)

reason: Encapsulated wellness product without curative claims fits the FSSAI Health Supplements / Nutraceuticals frame.
source: FSSAI (Health Supplements, Nutraceuticals, Food for Special Dietary Use...) Regulations, 2022

reason: Topical form with skin/hair care connotation maps to the Cosmetics Rules pathway.
Curative claims without a disclaimer signal an unregistered drug intent that must move to e-AUSHADHI licensing.
